startHere: Search this compact index by intent first.
Use the exact handle returned here; open AUTHORING_HANDLES.json only for the full card.
Treat Actor handles as identity/presentation only. Do not use Actor animation repertoires as the primary animation-authoring surface.

For animation, select an exact directAnimationMaterials[].animationHandle from CURRENT. Direct animation materials are authoritative even when Actor ownership is unresolved. Once explicitly selected for a cast subject, that exact handle remains the active visible animation across later consecutive beats while the subject stays visible, until another explicit animationHandle replaces it; carry-forward never selects a different animation.

Treat dialogue expressionIntent as opt-in, not a per-line default. Omit it for ordinary dialogue so the CharacterPack defaultExpression applies. Add it only for a deliberate visible acting beat, after resolving speaker to its cast identityHandle and requiring the token to be a literal member of that dialogueCharacters entry supportedExpressions; never auto-generate expressions from wording, mood or delivery, and never substitute Neutral.

When an intent has multiple animation candidates, open animationRetrievalPath and use its phase, sourcePath and preview evidence to choose deliberately; do not infer Start/Loop/End from a display name alone.

For every important visual choice, open previewUrl when present. previewUrl is authoring/QA evidence only, never runtime scene artwork: do not serialize it into V1 and never materialize an atlas/page preview as a Sprite or scene object. If previewUrl is missing, treat appearance as unverified instead of guessing from the name.

Use atlasPage/atlasSlot only as secondary browsing evidence. previewKind=ATLAS_PAGE_EVIDENCE_ONLY means the preview is a sheet/page reference for visual inspection, not the animation frame or runtime representation.

Use moves[] directly. It is the single first-class V1 directing vocabulary and exposes the currently registered legal move IDs. For every selected move, obey its phases, requiredRoles and cinematicSignature; the move id is never a decorative label.
Author exactly one CUTSCENE_SCRIPT_V1 object; never invent raw Catalog/runtime IDs.
